page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. The server features 64 dedicated vCPUs using AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU designed for compute-centric processing rather than memory-heavy footprints.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent file access and operational system disks. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. External networking capabilities feature a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

From an efficiency perspective, the high compute core density combined with moderate memory allocation provides a cost-effective platform for workloads that would underutilize higher memory-to-core ratios. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.16xlarge is suitable for CPU-bound tasks such as parallel compilation, distributed batch computing, web tier processing, application serving, and video transcoding.

The instance includes no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on external block storage for data persistence. This hardware allocation profile maximizes compute resource efficiency while reducing memory overhead. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.16xlarge is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, code compilation, video rendering, scientific simulation processing, and distributed microservices architectures.
